subsystems.name: Coronagraph optics
subsystems.role: Suppresses the star's light inside the telescope so a faint planet becomes visible.

subsystems.name: Wavefront control
subsystems.role: Measures and corrects optical errors to picometre stability, because any ripple leaks starlight.

subsystems.name: Starshade
subsystems.role: Flies tens of thousands of kilometres ahead and blocks the star before its light enters the telescope.

subsystems.name: Formation flying
subsystems.role: Keeps the starshade aligned with the telescope to within a metre over that distance.

subsystems.name: Telescope and platform
subsystems.role: Provides a stable, large aperture and points precisely at the target star.

subsystems.name: Spectrograph and data pipeline
subsystems.role: Splits the planet's light into a spectrum and separates it from residual starlight.

buildSteps.title: Model the diffraction
buildSteps.detail: Use computer simulations to design masks and pupils that push starlight away from where the planet appears.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the deformable mirror
buildSteps.detail: Build a mirror with hundreds or thousands of actuators that can bend its surface by fractions of a nanometre.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the coronagraph instrument
buildSteps.detail: Integrate the masks, mirrors, wavefront sensor and control electronics into a vacuum-sealed package.

buildSteps.title: Test in a space-like environment
buildSteps.detail: Run the instrument in a thermal-vacuum chamber to prove it holds alignment without air or gravity.

buildSteps.title: Build the starshade
buildSteps.detail: Manufacture a petal-shaped disc with edges accurate to tens of micrometres, so it blocks light without creating bright diffraction spikes.

buildSteps.title: Launch and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Fold the starshade for launch and unfold it in space once on the way to its observing position.

buildSteps.title: Practice formation flying
buildSteps.detail: Use thrusters and laser ranging to hold the starshade centred on the line between telescope and star, to within a metre at tens of thousands of kilometres.

buildSteps.title: Observe and analyse
buildSteps.detail: Point the telescope, block the star, and collect the planet's spectrum over hours to days.

prerequisites.tech: Deformable mirrors with thousands of actuators
prerequisites.why: already used in ground-based adaptive optics to correct atmospheric blur.

prerequisites.tech: Wavefront sensing and control at picometre stability
prerequisites.why: demonstrated in laboratory testbeds, but space-qualified systems are not yet flying.

prerequisites.tech: Starshade deployment and precision formation flying
prerequisites.why: no starshade has flown; it requires autonomous control at tens of thousands of kilometres.
Hubble and JWST show that large mirrors can hold shape in space.
used on ground-based and space coronagraphs to dig fainter planets out of residual starlight.

pathway.milestone: coronagraphs on Hubble, JWST and ground-based telescopes image young, massive planets
pathway.unlocks: first direct spectra of a few exoplanets.

pathway.milestone: a dedicated coronagraph on the Roman Space Telescope (planned) demonstrates imaging of Jupiter-like planets
pathway.unlocks: statistics on giant planets around nearby stars.

pathway.milestone: a starshade technology demonstration mission flies in formation with a space telescope
pathway.unlocks: proof that starshades work in space.

pathway.milestone: a large space telescope with a starshade images Earth-sized planets and looks for biosignatures
pathway.unlocks: direct study of potentially habitable worlds.
